approach: Static recompilation of the retail XBE to C++; XDK HLE with a Direct3D 12 renderer and XAudio2 on Windows, and a native Vulkan renderer with SDL3 on Linux (no Wine)
help: Naming the remaining genuinely unmatched XDK names in config/game.toml (7 crt_* math entries; the other 41 names at 0 are for sections this XBE does not have) and the graded D3D candidates in docs/d3d-gap-functions.md
Play-testing past the intro on Linux: menus, gameplay, saving and reloading have never been reached on screen
Hor+ ultrawide on the Vulkan backend: today the picture is pillarboxed at the title's own 4:3, and widening every viewport/scissor/2-D placement by the offset is its own piece of work
Building and testing the Windows target (Direct3D 12 + XAudio2): it has never been compiled, as the development machine has no MSVC or Windows SDK
Measuring the frame-step fix against the wall clock at high frame rates, entering the cheats in play, and exercising the keyboard/pad bindings in this game
notes: In bring-up, and it renders: the native Linux build (Vulkan + SDL3, no Wine) boots, mounts the disc, and plays the intro movie whole and correctly proportioned on a 3440x1440 display (pillarboxed at the game's own 4:3), with SDL3 audio and a measured 60 fps during video. The retail USA XBE (title id 0x45410043, built 2003-11-13 with XDK 5558) is extracted and identified, the SDK's XDK 5558 signature set was bootstrapped, config/game.toml names 194 of 242 symbols, and the XBE recompiles to 27,495 functions. Not proven: menus and gameplay past the intro, saving/reloading, the frame-step fix measured at high frame rates, cheats entered in play, the keyboard/pad bindings in this game, and Hor+ ultrawide (pillarboxed today). The Windows target has never been compiled. See docs/status.md for the evidence-cited state.
